newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian UDF wins 52 percent in election - official.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian UDF wins 52 percent in election - official.

text.p: Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces won 52.26 percent in Saturday's parliamentary election and will have 137 seats in the 240-seat parliament, final official results issued on Wednesday showed.
The former ruling Socialists won 22.07 percent and will have 58 seats. Three smaller parties will also enter parliament.

The Union for National Salvation, a coalition dominated by ethnic Turks and monarchists, will have 19 seats. The Euroleft, which includes many Socialist dissidents, will have 14, and the populist Bulgarian Business Bloc 12.

The UDF is expected to meet on Thursday to nominate party leader Ivan Kostov as prime minister, but formation of a new government may wait until after next week's four-day holiday for Eastern Orthodox Easter.
The new parliament is expected to hold its first session on May 5. The UDF wants all parties to agree on a declaration of principles for bringing the country out of its severe economic crisis.
